messages.subject: Help need for simulated extrapolation approach
parts:
Hello Distance sampling community,

I am seeking assistance with simulating an extrapolation approach to estimate abundance within a management unit. Some parts of the area are inaccessible to our preferred survey platform, so I'm exploring extrapolation techniques. Before field testing, I would like to simulate this approach. Currently, the plan is to sample randomly placed subplots using line transects and extrapolate to the whole area based on environmental covariates.

Firstly, I'd appreciate feedback on the general approach, as I've found limited information on this topic and am still unsure if it's feasible. What are the key considerations when it comes to extrapolation?

Secondly, I've struggled to find code examples for extrapolation. A paper described the `dsmextra` package, but I couldn't locate the actual code. Are there any code examples available for extrapolation?

Lastly, I attempted to run simulations with multiple strata study areas, as outlined in the appendix A here: [https://distancesampling.org/dssd/articles/MultiStrataVignette.html](https://distancesampling.org/dssd/articles/MultiStrataVignette.html). I managed to create transects within these strata, but my simulations always fail.
This is an reproducible code example where `run.survey()` fails when the simulation uses multi strata.

```
# Load the required library

library(dsims)

 

# Create a detectability function

detect_uf <- make.detectability(

  key.function = "uf",

  scale.param = 0.8,

  truncation = 2

)

 

# Define the outer boundary and holes for the polygons

outer <- matrix(c(0,0,15,0,15,10,0,10,0,0), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)

hole1 <- matrix(c(2,2,2,3,3,3,3,2,2,2), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)

hole2 <- matrix(c(5,5,5,6,7,6,8,5.5,7,5,5,5), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)

 

# Create polygons with holes

pol1 <- sf::st_polygon(list(outer, hole1*1.5, hole2))

pol2 <- sf::st_polygon(list(outer + 15, hole2*1.5 + 12))

pol3 <- sf::st_polygon(list(outer + 30, hole2*2.5 + 20))

 

# Combine polygons into a simple feature collection

sfc <- sf::st_sfc(pol1, pol2, pol3)

strata.names <- c("SW", "central", "NE")

mp1 <- sf::st_sf(strata = strata.names, geom = sfc)

 

# Print the simple feature collection

print(mp1)

 

# Define the study area

area_m <- matrix(c(0,0,45,0,45,40,0,40,0,0), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)

area <- sf::st_polygon(list(area_m))

 

# Plot the study area and the polygons

plot(area)

plot(mp1, add = TRUE)

 

# Create regions for the study area and subplots

study_region <- make.region(region.name = "study area", shape = area)

poly_region <- make.region(region.name = "sub plots", strata.name = strata.names, shape = mp1)

 

# Plot the regions

plot(study_region)

plot(poly_region)

 

# Create a flat density grid

density <- make.density(region = study_region, x.space = 1, constant = 1)

 

# Add hotspots to the density grid for spatial variability

density <- add.hotspot(object = density, centre = c(5, 5), sigma = 10, amplitude = 2)

density <- add.hotspot(object = density, centre = c(15, 25), sigma = 5, amplitude = 3)

density <- add.hotspot(object = density, centre = c(40, 15), sigma = 15, amplitude = -0.5)

 

# Plot the density grid

plot(density, study_region)

 

# Create a covariate list describing the distribution of cluster sizes

covariates <- list(cover = list(distribution = "ztruncpois", mean = 3))

 

# Create population descriptions for the study area and subplots

study_area_pop_desc_co <- make.population.description(region = study_region, density = density, covariates = covariates)

sub_plots_pop_desc_co <- make.population.description(region = poly_region, density = density, covariates = covariates)

 

# Create a systematic subplot design

subplots_design <- make.design(

  region = poly_region,

  transect.type = "line",

  design = "systematic",

  samplers = numeric(0), # OR

  line.length = numeric(0), # OR

  spacing = 3,

  design.angle = 0,

  edge.protocol = "minus",

  truncation = 2

)

 

# Generate transects for the subplot design

subplots_transects <- generate.transects(subplots_design)

 

# Plot the transects on the subplot region

plot(poly_region, subplots_transects, lwd = 0.5, col = 4)

 

# Create detection function analyses

ddf_analyses <- make.ds.analysis(dfmodel = ~1, key = c("hn", "hr"), criteria = "AIC", truncation = 2)

ddf_analyses_sub <- make.ds.analysis(dfmodel = ~1, key = c("hn", "hr"), criteria = "AIC", truncation = 2, group.strata = data.frame(design.id = poly_...@strata.name, analysis.id = rep("A", length(poly_...@strata.name))))

ddf_analyses_co <- make.ds.analysis(dfmodel = list(~1, ~1, ~cover, ~cover), key = c("hn", "hr", "hn", "hr"), criteria = "AIC", truncation = 2)

ddf_analyses_sub_co <- make.ds.analysis(dfmodel = list(~1, ~1, ~cover, ~cover), key = c("hn", "hr", "hn", "hr"), criteria = "AIC", truncation = 2, group.strata = data.frame(design.id = poly_...@strata.name, analysis.id = rep("A", length(poly_...@strata.name))))

 

# Create a simulation for the subplots

sim_sub <- make.simulation(

  reps = 99,

  design = subplots_design,

  population.description = sub_plots_pop_desc_co, # study_area_pop_desc_co, sub_plots_pop_desc_co

  detectability = detect_uf,

  ds.analysis = ddf_analyses_sub_co # ddf_analyses, ddf_analyses_sub, ddf_analyses_co, ddf_analyses_sub_co

)

 

# Run the survey and summarize the results

summary(sim_sub, use.max.reps = TRUE, description.summary = FALSE) # here were no successful repetitions.

 

# Failing

sub_survey <- run.survey(sim_sub) # Error in sample.int(length(x), size, replace, prob) : incorrect number of probabilities

 

# Print the survey results

print(sub_survey)

 

# Plot the survey results

plot(sub_survey, subplots)
```

BONUS questions: I'd like to assign a covariate to the individuals in the population based on their XY coordinates, to perform a sensitivity analysis of the effects of different levels of vegetation cover in the landscape.

Thank you very much for your time. Please let me know if you can provide guidance or share your experiences with these topics.

Best regards,  
Leonard

Welcome to the list. Quite a set of questions you have.

For model-based inference to be sound, the relationships found in modeling the data from the surveyed area is assumed to hold in the non-surveyed area. It is difficult to image how to assess that, given the non-surveyed area is inaccessible. Furthermore the distribution (in a statistical sense) of predictor covariates is assumed to be similar for the surveyed and non-surveyed areas. An example of a situation in which this would not hold: imagine the non-surveyed areas are inaccessible because they are extreme in altitude or terrain roughness. If those environmental covariates are used as predictors, it is unlikely the distributions will be similar in surveyed and non-surveyed areas.

Access to the code for the "dsmextra" package is described here

https://densitymodelling.github.io/dsmextra/

but I believe the package is no longer maintained. It depends on the deprecated "rgdal" package, which you might be able to install this way:

install.packages("rgdal", repos="http://R-Forge.R-project.org")


Next, for you "dsims" simulation code. I haven't parsed all of your code. I think I might start with something slightly simpler, to make debugging easier. I see you are trying to use group size as a covariate. However a glance at this help page:

?dsims::make.population.description

flags up this

covariates
Named list with one named entry per individual-level covariate. Cluster sizes can be defined here, it must be named 'size'.
whereas you have the line:

# Create a covariate list describing the distribution of cluster sizes
covariates <- list(cover = list(distribution = "ztruncpois", mean = 3))

The error message states some problem with "probabilities", which is a bit vague, but might point to problems with the population.description.

I also don't know how you want your detectability function to behave, you specify that it should be a uniform key function, but you provide a scale.param, which the uniform key does not possess.

Finally, regarding your bonus question (to demonstrate I read your email through to the end), I do not believe "dsims" has the ability to assign covariates based upon coordinates of the simulated objects. At least I've not seen a demonstration of such abilities.

Hello Eric,

Thanks for your reply.

Thank you for clarifying the model-based interference. We are planning to derive covariates from satellite produces, therefore we would know the statistical distribution of the covariates. The study area is mostly covered in the same vegetation type (boreal forest), we, which in our favor for the interference. But I appreciate you highlighting the limitations of interference. The question that arises for me, should one prioritize randomly placing subplots within the accessible area, or priorities placing the subplots to cover as much of the statics distribution of the covariates?

Thanks for pointing me to the dsmextra vignette. It is unfortunate that dsmextra is no longer maintained.

Regarding my `dsims` code, I tried to simply it and removed the inclusion of covariates. Furthermore, I split the code into two clear examples. One creating a population and density for a larger area, but the transects are only being placed in the sample areas. And the second created a population and density for each sample area. However, both fail when trying to run the simulation. If the issue lies with the population.description, then I do not know what to change. I tried different things with the same result.
The scale.param in the uniform key function adjust the detection rate. A scale.param of 0.8 assumes an 80% detection rate, due to account for that not all animals are available for detection all the time. The only reason I chose a uniform function in this example is to keep it simple. You can try other function, but in my testing, this did not make a difference.

Please use this simplified code for your testing. There is some repetition in the code to ensure that both example can be run independently of each other.

```
### Example 1: Creating density and population for study_region and run simulation

# Load the required library
library(dsims)
# Create Multi Strata Region

# Define the outer boundary and holes for the polygons
outer <- matrix(c(0,0,15,0,15,10,0,10,0,0), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)
hole1 <- matrix(c(2,2,2,3,3,3,3,2,2,2), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)
hole2 <- matrix(c(5,5,5,6,7,6,8,5.5,7,5,5,5), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)

# Create polygons with holes
pol1 <- sf::st_polygon(list(outer, hole1*1.5, hole2))
pol2 <- sf::st_polygon(list(outer + 15, hole2*1.5 + 12))
pol3 <- sf::st_polygon(list(outer + 30, hole2*2.5 + 20))

# Combine polygons into a simple feature collection
sfc <- sf::st_sfc(pol1, pol2, pol3)
strata.names <- c("SW", "central", "NE")
mp1 <- sf::st_sf(strata = strata.names, geom = sfc)

# Print the simple feature collection
print(mp1)

# Define the study area
area_m <- matrix(c(0,0,45,0,45,40,0,40,0,0), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)
area <- sf::st_polygon(list(area_m))

# Plot the study area and the polygons
plot(area)
plot(mp1, add = TRUE)

# Create regions for the study area and subplots
study_region <- make.region(region.name = "study area", shape = area)
poly_region <- make.region(region.name = "sub plots", strata.name = strata.names, shape = mp1)

# Plot the regions
plot(study_region)
plot(poly_region)

# Create a systematic subplot design
poly_design <- make.design(

region = poly_region,
  transect.type = "line",
  design = "systematic",
  samplers = numeric(0), # OR
  line.length = numeric(0), # OR
  spacing = 3,
  design.angle = 0,
  edge.protocol = "minus",
  truncation = 2
)
# Generate transects for the subplot design
poly_transects <- generate.transects(poly_design)
# Plot the transects on the subplot region

plot(poly_region, poly_transects, lwd = 0.5, col = 4)


## Create Density

# Create a flat density grid
density <- make.density(region = study_region, x.space = 1, constant = 1)

# Add hotspots to the density grid for spatial variability
density <- add.hotspot(object = density, centre = c(5, 5), sigma = 10, amplitude = 2)
density <- add.hotspot(object = density, centre = c(15, 25), sigma = 5, amplitude = 3)
density <- add.hotspot(object = density, centre = c(40, 15), sigma = 15, amplitude = -0.5)

# Plot the density grid

# Create population descriptions for the study area and subplots to test both

# Create a detectability function
detect_uf <- make.detectability(
  key.function = "uf",
  scale.param = 0.8,
  truncation = 2
)

# Create detection function analyses

# Create a simulation for the subplots

sim <- make.simulation(
  reps = 99,
  design = poly_design,
  population.description = study_area_pop_desc,

detectability = detect_uf,
  ds.analysis = ddf_analyses

)
# Run the survey and summarize the results

summary(sim, use.max.reps = TRUE, description.summary = FALSE) # here were no successful repetitions.

# Failing
survey <- run.survey(sim) # Error in sample.int(length(x), size, replace, prob) : incorrect number of probabilities
# Print the survey results
print(survey)
# Plot the survey results

plot(survey, study_region)

########################################################################################

### Example 2: Creating density and population only for poly_region and run simulation

# Load the required library
library(dsims)
# Create Multi Strata Region

# Define the outer boundary and holes for the polygons
outer <- matrix(c(0,0,15,0,15,10,0,10,0,0), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)
hole1 <- matrix(c(2,2,2,3,3,3,3,2,2,2), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)
hole2 <- matrix(c(5,5,5,6,7,6,8,5.5,7,5,5,5), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)

# Create polygons with holes
pol1 <- sf::st_polygon(list(outer, hole1*1.5, hole2))
pol2 <- sf::st_polygon(list(outer + 15, hole2*1.5 + 12))
pol3 <- sf::st_polygon(list(outer + 30, hole2*2.5 + 20))

# Combine polygons into a simple feature collection
sfc <- sf::st_sfc(pol1, pol2, pol3)
strata.names <- c("SW", "central", "NE")
mp1 <- sf::st_sf(strata = strata.names, geom = sfc)

# Print the simple feature collection
print(mp1)
# Create regions for the study area and subplots

poly_region <- make.region(region.name = "sub plots", strata.name = strata.names, shape = mp1)

# Plot the regions
plot(poly_region)
# Create a systematic subplot design
poly_design <- make.design(

region = poly_region,
  transect.type = "line",
  design = "systematic",
  samplers = numeric(0), # OR
  line.length = numeric(0), # OR
  spacing = 3,
  design.angle = 0,
  edge.protocol = "minus",
  truncation = 2
)
# Generate transects for the subplot design
poly_transects <- generate.transects(poly_design)
# Plot the transects on the subplot region

plot(poly_region, poly_transects, lwd = 0.5, col = 4)

## Create Density
# Create a flat density grid
density_poly <- make.density(region = poly_region, x.space = 1, constant = 1)
# Add hotspots to the density grid for spatial variability

density_poly <- add.hotspot(object = density_poly, centre = c(5, 5), sigma = 10, amplitude = 2)
density_poly <- add.hotspot(object = density_poly, centre = c(15, 25), sigma = 5, amplitude = 3)
density_poly <- add.hotspot(object = density_poly, centre = c(40, 15), sigma = 15, amplitude = -0.5)
# Plot the density grid

plot(density_poly, poly_region)

# Create population descriptions for the study area and subplots to test both
poly_pop_desc <- make.population.description(region = poly_region, density = density_poly)

# Create a detectability function
detect_uf <- make.detectability(
  key.function = "uf",
  scale.param = 0.8,
  truncation = 2
)
plot(detect_uf, poly_pop_desc)
# Create detection function analyses

ddf_analyses_poly <- make.ds.analysis(dfmodel = ~1, key = c("hn", "hr"), criteria = "AIC", truncation = 2, group.strata = data.frame(design.id = poly_region@strata.name, analysis.id = rep("A", length(poly_region@strata.name))))
# Create a simulation for the subplots

poly_sim <- make.simulation(
  reps = 99,
  design = poly_design,
  population.description = poly_pop_desc,
  detectability = detect_uf,
  ds.analysis = ddf_analyses_poly

)

# Run the survey and summarize the results

summary(poly_sim, use.max.reps = TRUE, description.summary = FALSE) # here were no successful repetitions.

# Failing
poly_survey <- run.survey(poly_sim) # Error in sample.int(length(x), size, replace, prob) : incorrect number of probabilities
# Print the survey results
print(poly_survey)
# Plot the survey results

plot(poly_survey, poly_region)
```

Welcome to the list. Quite a set of questions you have.

For model-based inference to be sound, the relationships found in modeling the data from the surveyed area is assumed to hold in the non-surveyed area. It is difficult to image how to assess that, given the non-surveyed area is inaccessible. Furthermore the distribution (in a statistical sense) of predictor covariates is assumed to be similar for the surveyed and non-surveyed areas. An example of a situation in which this would not hold: imagine the non-surveyed areas are inaccessible because they are extreme in altitude or terrain roughness. If those environmental covariates are used as predictors, it is unlikely the distributions will be similar in surveyed and non-surveyed areas.

Access to the code for the "dsmextra" package is described here

https://densitymodelling.github.io/dsmextra/

but I believe the package is no longer maintained. It depends on the deprecated "rgdal" package, which you might be able to install this way:

install.packages("rgdal", repos="http://R-Forge.R-project.org")


Next, for you "dsims" simulation code. I haven't parsed all of your code. I think I might start with something slightly simpler, to make debugging easier. I see you are trying to use group size as a covariate. However a glance at this help page:

?dsims::make.population.description

flags up this

covariates
Named list with one named entry per individual-level covariate. Cluster sizes can be defined here, it must be named 'size'.
whereas you have the line:

# Create a covariate list describing the distribution of cluster sizes
covariates <- list(cover = list(distribution = "ztruncpois", mean = 3))

The error message states some problem with "probabilities", which is a bit vague, but might point to problems with the population.description.

I also don't know how you want your detectability function to behave, you specify that it should be a uniform key function, but you provide a scale.param, which the uniform key does not possess.

Finally, regarding your bonus question (to demonstrate I read your email through to the end), I do not believe "dsims" has the ability to assign covariates based upon coordinates of the simulated objects. At least I've not seen a demonstration of such abilities.

Welcome to the list. Quite a set of questions you have.

For model-based inference to be sound, the relationships found in modeling the data from the surveyed area is assumed to hold in the non-surveyed area. It is difficult to image how to assess that, given the non-surveyed area is inaccessible. Furthermore the distribution (in a statistical sense) of predictor covariates is assumed to be similar for the surveyed and non-surveyed areas. An example of a situation in which this would not hold: imagine the non-surveyed areas are inaccessible because they are extreme in altitude or terrain roughness. If those environmental covariates are used as predictors, it is unlikely the distributions will be similar in surveyed and non-surveyed areas.

Access to the code for the "dsmextra" package is described here

https://densitymodelling.github.io/dsmextra/

but I believe the package is no longer maintained. It depends on the deprecated "rgdal" package, which you might be able to install this way:

install.packages("rgdal", repos="http://R-Forge.R-project.org")


Next, for you "dsims" simulation code. I haven't parsed all of your code. I think I might start with something slightly simpler, to make debugging easier. I see you are trying to use group size as a covariate. However a glance at this help page:

?dsims::make.population.description

flags up this

covariates
Named list with one named entry per individual-level covariate. Cluster sizes can be defined here, it must be named 'size'.
whereas you have the line:
